result:
Round 280 **passes**, and nothing goes back to B as a bug. I re-ran every check myself, all 13 of my rows pass, and I changed no app source.

This was a test-only round. It changes how the export performance test counts memory samples inside the export time window, so the Studio itself did not change.

- **Changed files:** the two perf files are byte-identical to B's planned sketch. The frozen-file checksums matched at the start and at the end, and every changed file is one A was allowed to touch.
- **Perf run:** passed in 1.3 minutes, run with nothing else on the machine. Typecheck also passes.
- **Comparison with B's baseline run:** 0 problems and 0 tolerated differences across 61 rows. The new sample counts are never below the old rule's, and the run counted 11 more samples in total across its 12 exports. The task required at least 3.
- **Clock check:** the clock check's round trip was 1–3 ms in every export, well under the 20 ms limit, and the clock offset stayed within 2 ms.
- **Budget notes:** all 8 changed notes match the task text exactly, and no other field changed. My first comparison showed a false mismatch because my own pattern was wrong; the corrected check is in the same file.
- **Mutants:** I rebuilt the four mutants from A's actual files rather than from A's diff. Each gave its expected signal:
  - the sign flip drops every sample to 0;
  - restoring the old rule gives a difference of exactly 0;
  - the control version passes the comparison;
  - the probe that throws aborts every pass at the first export with no leak message.
- **Auth, in a real browser at 1440×900 and 1280×720:**
  - the demo page opens with no sign-in;
  - the protected Studio page shows "Sign in required" and loads no audio;
  - the token endpoint returns 401 with no token.

  The first 1440×900 attempt timed out after 150 s while the dev server was still warming up, the same issue as round 279. I kept it as evidence and its one allowed retry passed.
- **Docs:** the status lines in docs 209, 208 and 176 are exact. Doc 209's sample ranges match A's two runs, and every id it cites exists.
- **Extra check (not counted as a round row):** playback works at both viewports, and the exported 16-second WAV is bit-identical to round 279's. That fits with no app code having changed.

The full test suite, build, Biome, `npm run verify` and the e2e smoke test are left to the root gate and are not claimed.

The memory-polls headroom issue (R216) stays a watch item: the new rule adds about one sample per export, and the lowest single-clip count was 9 against the floor of 5.

Files are in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- c-round-280.md
- c-round-280.json
- c-round-280/
